$comment: The development subtree. Unlike the vendor subtrees this is not a specification reference: its sources are kernel commits, project issue trackers, vendor security bulletins and measurements taken on real silicon. archChapter is therefore deliberately unmatchable, so a claim here is not required to carry a Tier-1 specification anchor - it must still carry a resolvable [N], a confidence and a volatility, and it may carry a vendor anchor when one genuinely applies. Demanding an anchor a subject cannot supply is how ~90 fabricated anchors once entered this corpus; see README.
$comment_archChapter: Never matches. See above - this subtree cites implementations and measurements, not specifications.
$comment_anchors: Both vendors' grammars are legal here, because a development claim routinely cites one vendor's manual while discussing the other's divergence. The `measured` form is new in v2 and is the shape agreed for an on-metal observation: it must carry the CPUID signature, the firmware level and the date, because an observation missing any of the three cannot be reproduced and is therefore not evidence.
$comment_unscopedNegative: Identical to the vendor subtrees. The defect class is not vendor-specific, and a development chapter is exactly where 'no public X exists' gets written carelessly about a tool or a project rather than a specification.

patterns.re: (there (?:is|are) no public |\b(?:AMD|Intel|Microsoft|the vendor) publishes no \b|\b(?:AMD|Intel|Microsoft) has no public \b|\bno public [a-z\- ]{0,40}(?:guide|reference|PPR|document|documentation|specification|erratum|errata|copy|source) )

unscopedNegative.message: a negative claim needs the same evidence as a positive one, scoped to a document and a date (see references/amd/errata.md E27)

$comment_eval: 20 questions, not 80. This subtree carries 23 claims; a set padded to the vendor sets' size would test invention rather than recall. Two of its four types are new in v2 - build questions are scored against the trap list rather than for resemblance, and gap questions score full marks for correctly naming what the corpus cannot determine.
